bounded_predicate: Opt-in output policy: a dumpStack call-name with receiver text exactly Thread reports the KtCallExpression only; catch-body descendant names equal to the catch parameter report that receiver-name entity when nextSibling.nextSibling is a call whose text starts printStackTrace(. No rule-specific options or destination/type/alias analysis.

positive.intent: Exercise both actual entity shapes on valid JVM spellings: direct Thread.dumpStack reports only dumpStack(), while a caught throwable printStackTrace reports only its failure receiver. Both violate the explicitly selected output convention, not a proved confidentiality property.

negative.intent: Use caller-controlled recording/report callbacks instead of the two direct stack-print spellings. The rule stays active; absence of this warning is not proof that the callbacks redact, persist, or handle failure correctly.

suppression.intent: Genuine file-scoped upstream suppression only on the package-isolated copy. Preserve every positive range from the byte-identical unsuppressed neighbor. No host finding filter or ktChecker-ID suppression alias.

controls.intent: This private non-JDK Thread object returns a benign work-name list; it does not print a stack trace. The exact receiver/call spelling still matches. Retain the anticipated false positive caused by absent type resolution.

The caught throwable is still directly printed, but through a local alias rather than a receiver named exactly like the catch parameter. Preserve the anticipated false negative; alias flow is not inspected.

The real JDK java.lang.Thread.dumpStack still prints a stack dump, but the receiver text is qualified rather than exactly Thread. Retain this anticipated false negative instead of treating qualification as safe logging.

limitations: This is explicit opt-in info/policy/intent-dependent output style. Direct diagnostics can be intentional and destination policy must be decided by the owner.
The Thread branch reports the call expression without its receiver. The caught-throwable branch reports the receiver-name reference, not the method name or whole qualified call.
A same-spelled non-JDK Thread is an anticipated false positive. A local caught-throwable alias and fully qualified JDK Thread are independently retained anticipated false negatives.
Printing outside a catch, whitespace/sibling forms, nested same-named receivers and other output mechanisms are not fully covered. No exhaustive call or type resolution is claimed.
Stream/writer destinations, log retention, secrets, taint and redaction are not evaluated. This is not an information-disclosure, security or safe-logging certificate.
No rule-specific options exist. No parser/compiler, semantic, cancellation, ownership, model, natural-project or release qualification is claimed.

six_case_plan.positive: Run the exact owner-selected syntax route on these immutable source bytes. Expected ranges are authored from the pinned predicate, never observed output.
six_case_plan.negative: Run the independent valid alternative with this SAME rule active and require an enabled upstream descriptor even with no finding.
six_case_plan.configuration: Replay original positive bytes with the selected rule explicitly disabled. This is a separately counted configuration control, never a scope/default-activation reduction.
six_case_plan.version: Replay positive bytes under the pinned CLI; require a fresh per-cohort version probe and two per-rule Common/Native abstentions. Modeled baseline 2.4.21 versus parser 2.4.10 remains unqualified.
six_case_plan.suppression: Use genuine upstream file annotation only on an additional package-isolated copy; the unsuppressed original neighbor must keep every expected range.
six_case_plan.regression: Seal the negative correction as the child of suppression, delete the obsolete suppressed copy, and verify both registered parent and child unchanged.

qualification_note: Authored ranges/intents are not observed diagnostics. Retain unexpected/false-positive outputs and all misses; never rewrite expectations to force a pass. All three rules require explicit owner opt-in and retain info/intent-dependent classification. Real isolated runner, active descriptor, source snapshots and fresh source-bound evidence require separate root admission. No natural-project, parser, semantic, ownership, cancellation-flow, taint, redaction, model or release qualification.
